papers.title: Learning-based Attitude Estimation with Noisy Measurements and Unknown Gyro Bias
papers.authors: Parham Oveissi; Mohammad Mirtaba; Ankit Goel
papers.why: Gyroscope integration drifts under unknown bias; an SO(3) filter must correct the rotation without breaking its manifold structure.
papers.method: Retrospective Cost Attitude Estimator (RCAE): propagate rotation with the measured angular increment and apply a multiplicative correction tuned by retrospective-cost adaptive control. The correction avoids the MEKF measurement Jacobian and does not explicitly estimate gyro bias.
papers.math: R_{k+1} = R_k exp([omega_m]x Delta t) exp([u_k]x), with the second exponential a data-adaptive correction; note the paper's measured orientation input rather than reducing it to a gravity-only observation.
papers.evidence: Numerical simulations and physical attitude-estimation comparisons with a multiplicative EKF are described in the primary paper. No matched TG-DCM dataset or tilt metric is published.
papers.limits: Crucial task mismatch: the estimator is provided noisy orientation measurements, not only a six-axis acceleration/gyro stream; do not call it a six-axis-only competitive baseline without replacing that measurement channel.
papers.transfer: Consider multiplicative/SO(3) correction or retrospective adaptation as a separately benchmarked filter head; preserve the gravity-only yaw gauge.

papers.title: A robust adaptive error state Kalman filter for MEMS IMU attitude estimation under dynamic acceleration
papers.authors: Xiaofeng Wei; Shiwei Fan; Ya Zhang; Wei Gao; Feng Shen; Xie Ming; Jian Yang
papers.why: Acceleration beyond gravity corrupts roll/pitch correction in conventional inertial attitude filters.
papers.method: Nominal direction-cosine matrix plus small error-state filter; adaptive disturbance handling switches between explicit dynamic-acceleration compensation and measurement-noise covariance adjustment according to monitored motion thresholds.
papers.math: R_true approximately R_nom exp([delta theta]x). The EKF updates a local error state instead of adding nine independent DCM components; dynamic acceleration changes measurement residual reliability.
papers.evidence: Publisher abstract reports at least 42.76% pitch and 67.21% roll improvement in selected dynamic experiments, but these are authors' scenario-specific comparisons, not results on the TG-DCM benchmark.
papers.limits: Full methods and data tables not acquired; threshold sensitivity, motion-distribution shift and covariance-consistency properties remain unverified; no implementation inspected.
papers.transfer: Implement as direct six-axis baseline with identical preprocessing, calibration, per-sequence tilt metrics and time-window latency.

papers.title: EqNIO: Subequivariant Neural Inertial Odometry
papers.authors: Royina Karegoudra Jayanth; Yinshuang Xu; Ziyun Wang; Evangelos Chatzipantazis; Daniel Gehrig; Kostas Daniilidis
papers.why: The same pedestrian motion expressed in different yaw-aligned sensor frames otherwise forces a learned odometry network to memorize redundant directions.
papers.method: Build gravity-aligned equivariant vector and invariant scalar representations; learn an O(2)-subequivariant canonical frame and rotate IMU features into it; regress displacement/covariance in canonical coordinates then transform predictions back.
papers.math: For gravity-preserving Q, mu(QX)=Q mu(X) and Sigma(QX)=Q Sigma(X) Q^T. Under reflections, gyroscope angular velocity is axial rather than polar, requiring the appropriate parity handling.
papers.evidence: Paper evaluates TLIO, Aria, RIDI, OxIOD and a RoNIN-derived model; repository implements vector-neuron network primitives and probabilistic displacement loss. Odometry ATE is not attitude tilt RMSE.
papers.limits: Requires a gravity-aligned reference; the choice of subgroup and canonicalization can hide sensitivity to inaccurate estimated vertical. Its specific O(2) symmetry is not automatically arbitrary SO(3) remount equivariance.
papers.transfer: Derive a causal SO(3)-covariant tilt correction on S^2 without needing an externally supplied attitude estimate; use exact remount tests.

papers.title: DIVE: Deep Inertial-Only Velocity Aided Estimation for Quadrotors
papers.authors: Angad Bajwa; Charles Champagne Cossette; Mohammed Ayman Shalaby; James Richard Forbes
papers.why: A quadrotor can lose camera tracking and pure IMU double integration then produces rapidly diverging navigation estimates.
papers.method: Regress three-axis velocity from causal IMU history and use it as an update in an on-manifold extended Kalman filter.
papers.math: The learned virtual velocity measurement supplies an innovation to a geometric filter; errors in gyro bias still propagate through its nominal attitude and velocity dynamics.
papers.evidence: Authors report 42% better localization on in-distribution flights, 22% OOD and 43% over dead reckoning in a VIO-failure scenario; no matched six-axis tilt benchmark.
papers.limits: Trajectory metrics and flight distribution are different from tilt estimation. Full implementation was not inspected.
papers.transfer: Learned pseudo-measurement integrated into geometric filter, with an explicit measurement noise and testable innovation consistency.

papers.title: On the effects of angular acceleration in orientation estimation using inertial measurement units
papers.authors: Felix Brändle; David Meister; Marc Seidel; Robin Strässer; Frank Allgöwer
papers.why: Low-cost IMU orientation estimation fails during rotational acceleration, even when gravity is predictable at the body origin.
papers.method: Derive transfer functions including accelerometer displacement from a rotation center, then analyze Mahony/Madgwick feedback and nonminimum-phase operating regimes.
papers.math: Rigid-sensor acceleration contains alpha x r + omega x (omega x r). Linearized transfer zeros can enter the right half plane depending on lever arm and operating point; lowering feedback gain trades tracking bandwidth for disturbance attenuation.
papers.evidence: Analytical model, numerical/experimental study of tracking vs bandwidth, with explicit orientation-filter consequences.
papers.limits: Linearization and platform geometry determine when predictions apply; does not provide a general learned attitude estimator or globally optimal filter.
papers.transfer: Include lever-arm-controlled dynamic acceleration and closed-loop bandwidth in evaluation; mere accelerometer norm gating is insufficient.

papers.title: AirIO: Learning Inertial Odometry with Enhanced IMU Feature Observability
papers.authors: Yuheng Qiu and collaborators
papers.why: Rotating IMU acceleration into a gravity/world frame can discard informative body-motion interactions in aerial dynamics.
papers.method: Learn body-frame motion using temporal CNN + recurrent features; compare versions with explicit attitude input, predict velocity and heteroscedastic uncertainty and fuse through an estimator.
papers.math: Rather than collapsing the input to world-frame specific force, body-frame a and omega are retained, and a learned covariance conditions downstream filter updates.
papers.evidence: Authors' ablations and published aerial trajectory results; inspected actual CNNEncoder, CodeNetMotion/CodeNetMotionwithRot and training/evaluation entry points.
papers.limits: An attitude-aided network is not six-axis standalone without explaining how attitude is obtained; reported translation metrics are not tilt metrics, and sensor remounting is not automatically equivariant.
papers.transfer: Compare body-frame temporal context with gravity-aligned processing and uncertainty-conditioned updates; avoid importing an unavailable attitude input.

papers.title: Tartan IMU: A Light Foundation Model for Inertial Positioning in Robotics
papers.authors: Shibo Zhao and collaborators
papers.why: Models tied to one device, embodiment or dataset generalize poorly to other locomotion and sensor domains.
papers.method: Cross-platform IMU feature pretraining, lightweight ResNet-LSTM trunk and platform-specific output heads with efficient adaptation.
papers.math: The shared sequence encoder maps sensor windows to latent motion representations; per-platform heads predict motion and are fine-tuned instead of retraining all parameters.
papers.evidence: CVPR paper reports multi-platform experiments and adaptation; released Python code contains registered LSTM Foundation_Model but its Transformer builder explicitly raises NotImplementedError because that core was not released.
papers.limits: The public Transformer implementation is not available in the inspected revision; its inertial positioning targets and velocity/trajectory metrics differ from roll/pitch.
papers.transfer: Pretrain a compact causal encoder over heterogeneous IMU devices, evaluate adaptation by held-out device and mount; release exact inference core and checkpoints.

papers.title: iMoT: Inertial Motion Transformer for Inertial Navigation
papers.authors: Son Minh Nguyen; Duc Viet Le; Paul J. M. Havinga
papers.why: Long-range attention alone may obscure local motion transitions and desynchronized gyro/accelerometer interactions.
papers.method: Transformer with a Progressive Series Decoupler, adaptive positional encoding across inertial modalities, learned query motion particles, and dynamic particle scoring for segment-level velocity.
papers.math: Attention and query-particle aggregation model multiple plausible motions, rather than maintaining only a single deterministic recurrent state.
papers.evidence: AAAI publication evaluated navigation/trajectory accuracy; GitHub publication listing observed but operational model code not verified.
papers.limits: Non-causal/future-window characteristics and computational budget cannot be assumed compatible with instant tilt tracking; trajectory targets only.
papers.transfer: Treat multi-resolution temporal encoders as a controlled ablation; demand lookahead/latency budgets and same sensor channels.

papers.title: Learned IMU Bias Prediction for Invariant Visual Inertial Odometry
papers.authors: Abdullah Altawaitan; Jason Stanley; Sambaran Ghosal; Thai Duong; Nikolay Atanasov
papers.why: Unknown, slowly drifting gyro/accelerometer bias contaminates integration and complicates invariant filter symmetry.
papers.method: Predict IMU bias from historical sensor windows using a learned model, then feed corrected measurements into an invariant MSCKF instead of adding bias as an ordinary group-state component.
papers.math: omega_corr = omega_m - bhat_g(x_history), a_corr = a_m - bhat_a(x_history); geometric propagation remains separate from a learned nuisance-state estimate.
papers.evidence: Real visual-inertial tests include periods of visual outage; does not establish unassisted six-axis gravity-only yaw accuracy.
papers.limits: VIO evaluation assumes images during some segments and a particular filter state/observability structure; bias estimates may entangle motion cues if not regularized.
papers.transfer: Explore slow-time-scale bias state and uncertainty without supervising spurious absolute yaw, with rest, thermal, and time-drift tests.

papers.title: IONext: Unlocking the Next Era of Inertial Odometry
papers.authors: Shanshan Zhang and collaborators
papers.why: Pure Transformers can miss high-frequency local motion detail despite their long-range receptive field.
papers.method: CNN-style Dual-wing Adaptive Dynamic Mixer combines global and local motion features; Spatio-Temporal Gating Unit selects temporally relevant events.
papers.math: Input-conditioned multi-scale mixing and temporal gating act as a selective motion representation, not a physical attitude observer.
papers.evidence: Authors report six inertial navigation datasets and average ATE/RTE improvements over iMoT on an RNIN split; no TG-DCM tilt evidence.
papers.limits: Main task is inertial odometry. Code, matched latency and OOD sensor-mount effects were not verified.
papers.transfer: Test small multi-rate temporal convolutions vs the GRU under fixed parameter count/streaming latency.

papers.title: Effects of Gyroscope Bias Augmentation on Recurrent Neural Network Model Performance for Attitude Estimation
papers.authors: Ji Hoon Park; Chang June Lee; Jung Keun Lee
papers.why: Gyroscope bias sensitivity damages recurrent six-axis attitude estimators and synthetic bias augmentation may be insufficiently characterized.
papers.method: Investigate recurrent model performance when training gyro signals are augmented with bias perturbations. Detailed architecture/protocol unavailable in this review.
papers.math: Synthetic omega_train = omega_measured + b_sample, with b_sample distribution and temporal correlation requiring confirmation against paper methods.
papers.evidence: Publisher DOI and abstract were located; quantitative findings, experiment setup and paper tables were not independently checked.
papers.limits: Do not infer optimal bias distribution, improvement magnitude or model choice without full text.
papers.transfer: Run controlled constant/random-walk/temperature-proxy gyro bias ablations and report separate device OOD performance.

papers.title: A deep learning framework for robust attitude estimation in dynamic environments from six-axis raw inertial measurements
papers.authors: Wei Ding; Yansen Hu; Wei Sun; Zhe Yue
papers.why: Fixed-gain filters and gyro integration perform poorly under dynamic acceleration and raw-sensor distribution shifts.
papers.method: Residual temporal CNN feature extractor joined to bidirectional LSTM context; normalized quaternion output from raw 3-axis accel + 3-axis gyro, with bounded lookahead.
papers.math: The network maps a time window a_{t-w:t+l}, omega_{t-w:t+l} to qhat_t; l>0 incurs algorithmic lookahead and must be accounted for when comparing causal systems.
papers.evidence: Publisher abstract claims median attitude error under 3 degrees and over 10% improvement against selected baselines; lacks same-split TG-DCM comparison or accessible full results here.
papers.limits: Full text inaccessible; detailed loss, dataset splits, runtime and available code not verified. Bidirectionality prohibits treating the output as zero-lookahead without an explicit buffer policy.
papers.transfer: Highest-priority direct modern comparator: reproduce on same six-axis datasets at matched latency and same yaw-invariant tilt RMSE.

papers.title: A Physics-Informed Dual-Branch LSTM Network for UAV Position and Attitude Estimation
papers.authors: Authors as listed in journal DOI
papers.why: Pure regression of UAV position and orientation ignores rigid-body kinematic coupling and drift-inducing physical inconsistency.
papers.method: Shared temporal LSTM encoder with separate position and quaternion attitude branches; kinematic losses include attitude propagation, coordinate transform, velocity-position integration and initial-state constraints.
papers.math: Use quaternion kinematics q_{t+1} approximately q_t tensor Exp(omega_t Delta t / 2) and p_{t+1}=p_t+v_t Delta t, with additional world/body acceleration transformation. Published loss specifics require separate reproduction.
papers.evidence: Open-access full text obtained through scholarly connector; UZH-FPV Drone Racing evaluations, position RMSE 0.0654 m in stated experiment, plus ablations. The paper explicitly assumes dataset-provided initial reference state and neglects explicit online gyro drift compensation.
papers.limits: Absolute position cannot be maintained from an unconstrained six-axis IMU without additional assumptions/prior; short-sequence, initialized evaluation is not a proof of arbitrary-duration drift-free inertial navigation. Position RMSE is not tilt.
papers.transfer: Use branch-specific constrained losses only where auxiliary state variables and reference initialization are available and auditable.

papers.title: MoRPI-PINN: a physics-informed framework for mobile robot pure inertial navigation
papers.authors: Arup Kumar Sahoo; Itzik Klein
papers.why: Pure 2D inertial integration is highly sensitive to noise and gyro/accelerometer bias.
papers.method: Encode 2D inertial navigation differential equations as training residuals alongside data and initial-condition constraints; exploit controlled snake-like robot motion.
papers.math: L = lambda_data L_data + lambda_phys ||d xhat/dt - f_INS(xhat,u)||^2 + lambda_init L_init, with paper-specific term details and scaling to be checked in exact reproduction.
papers.evidence: Real robot study over six trajectories reports position error 4.2m vs 68.6m for 2D INS and 22.1m for MoRPINet, under the study's specific motion setup.
papers.limits: Snake-like motion is a deliberate observability/denoising assumption; no direct evidence of general SO(3) attitude improvement and no public code evaluated here.
papers.transfer: A physically consistent, learnable update is preferable to unconstrained regression when physical state/assumptions are explicitly modeled.

papers.title: AI-IO: An Aerodynamics-Inspired Real-Time Inertial Odometry for Quadrotors
papers.authors: Jiahao Cui; Feng Yu; Linzuo Zhang; Yu Hu; Danping Zou
papers.why: For quadrotors, body velocity may be poorly identified from accelerometer and gyro history without modeling aerodynamic drag and thrust.
papers.method: Combine inertial sensors with rotor speed to make drag/thrust more informative, use CNN features + transformer encoder to predict velocity/uncertainty, fuse with uncertainty-aware EKF.
papers.math: Authors model a_x approximately -lambda_x omega_m^2 v_x - k1 v_x - k2 v_x^2 + bias + noise; using omega_m (motor speed) changes input observability relative to six-axis IMU.
papers.evidence: Authors report 36.9% gain from rotor speed and 22.4% additional gain from architecture in velocity prediction; inspected actual IMUTransformerWithModality and heteroscedastic Gaussian loss.
papers.limits: Not IMU-only in the strict six-axis setting; windless or simplified aerodynamic assumptions and platform-specific rotor information limit transfer.
papers.transfer: Use as justification for declaring observability assumptions and testing conditional side-channel sensing, not as a strict six-axis tilt baseline.

papers.title: KISS-IMU: Self-supervised Inertial Odometry with Motion-balanced Learning and Uncertainty-aware Inference
papers.authors: Jiwon Choi; Hogyun Kim; Geonmo Yang; Juhui Lee; Younggun Cho
papers.why: Collecting exact navigation ground truth across motion types is costly; common slow motions dominate training and rare rapid turns fail.
papers.method: Use LiDAR ICP registration and pose-graph optimization as pseudo-supervision during training; motion feature Gaussian mixtures balance training and adaptive uncertainty weighting governs inference.
papers.math: For motion-component k with empirical density p(k), increase relative weight of underrepresented k subject to clipping; correct the neural integration using uncertainty-based factor weights.
papers.evidence: Authors demonstrate quadruped and other motion datasets; inspected sklearn GaussianMixture implementation, mixture-based weighting, covariance weight controller, and PyPose integrator.
papers.limits: Not sensor-only self-supervision during training: LiDAR supplies the target; teacher ICP failure can bias pseudo-labels. Translational error metrics do not establish tilt improvement.
papers.transfer: Use motion-component balancing and per-motion robustness assessments, with correct group-level split to avoid near-duplicate leakage.

papers.title: GINIO: A Geometric SO(3)-Equivariant Interface for Neural Inertial Odometry
papers.authors: Chankyo Kim; Minghan Zhu; Tzu-Yuan Lin; Avantika Rattan; Maani Ghaffari
papers.why: Rotating or remounting the IMU should transform motion means/covariances predictably; ordinary sensor-frame networks violate the geometric law.
papers.method: SO(3)-equivariant vector-neuron convolution/GRU and geometry-aware outputs; Last-Frame Alignment (LFA) for equivariant models; spectral covariance parameterization transported by congruence.
papers.math: m(QZ)=Qm(Z) and Sigma(QZ)=Q Sigma(Z) Q^T. In vector-neuron GRU, update/reset gates are invariant scalars and hidden features are 3-vectors transformed equivariantly.
papers.evidence: Paper reports TLIO, NanoBench and Fetch remount robustness and ATE (meters); actual repository includes code and an author-side docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md audit documenting several paper-to-checkpoint discrepancies.
papers.limits: Important evidence failures in public erratum: some printed covariance NLL/NEES values lack measured support; an LFA-labeled checkpoint was trained without LFA; a NanoBench comparison mixed TLIO-pretrained and NanoBench-trained models; with-attitude input is not equivariant under certain physical remount transformations; some rotation robustness cells lack generators or reuse different weights. Do NOT present all paper tables as reproduced.
papers.transfer: Evaluate *actual* SO(3) remount transformations including attitude-channel transformation and covariance; demand checkpoint hashes, settings and regeneration scripts for every published cell.

papers.title: Motion-Acceleration Calibration and Compensation in IMUs without External Equipment for Attitude Estimation Filters
papers.authors: Fabian Arzberger; Andreas Nüchter
papers.why: When IMU is not at the rotation center, tangential and centripetal acceleration contaminate the apparent gravity direction and confidence gating alone discards potentially recoverable information.
papers.method: Calibrate accelerometer/gyro scale, bias, axis misalignment, IMU-to-pivot lever arm and optionally multi-IMU extrinsics from multiposition/static-and-rotation maneuvers; subtract modeled rotational accelerations online.
papers.math: a_sensor = a_origin + alpha x r + omega x (omega x r). Given r and estimates of omega and alpha, remove the last two terms before gravitational tilt correction.
papers.evidence: Primary arXiv HTML contains derivations, simulation and real spherical-mobile-system experiments; authors link open-source code and calibration data at fallow24/ros_imu_calib. This particular code was not inspected.
papers.limits: Needs fixed/known pivot model over calibration motion; differentiating gyro to obtain alpha amplifies noise; cannot remove arbitrary translational acceleration from IMU alone.
papers.transfer: Add calibrated deterministic rotational acceleration compensation ahead of a learned confidence gate, and report the assumptions and failure modes.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Inertial Odometry
papers.authors: Yuheng Qiu; Yutian Chen; Carlton Cort; Weison Huang; Shibo Zhao; Pieter Abbeel; Rocky Duan; Koushil Sreenath; C. Karen Liu; Carmelo Sferrazza; Junyi Geng; Sebastian Scherer; Guanya Shi
papers.why: Each new robot embodiment needs expensive ground-truth trajectory labels before learning a motion prior.
papers.method: Integration self-supervision: a myopic IMU preintegration teacher creates short-window velocity-change targets, a context-rich student denoises them, and pose-graph distillation then produces sequence-consistent targets.
papers.math: Teacher Delta v over a short window is obtained by IMU preintegration; student trained on many windows can average teacher noise under recurrent motion priors, then optimize with graph-consistent pseudo-labels.
papers.evidence: Authors evaluate six datasets and report average velocity error within 0.07 m/s of matched supervised baselines; no dedicated tilt RMSE evidence.
papers.limits: The teacher may inherit gyro/acceleration bias; student gains depend on repeated embodiment dynamics and sufficient excitation. Self-supervision alone cannot create an absolute yaw reference.
papers.transfer: Try physics-generated tilt consistency pseudo-targets only with explicit identifiability analysis and controlled bias/linear-acceleration tests.

papers.title: MosaicIMU: Composing Carrier Experts for Generalizable Neural Inertial Odometry
papers.authors: Junye Zou; Huiyi Yan; Xinning Xu; Xiaolei Li; Pengkun Zhou; Jinhui Zhang; Ziyang Meng
papers.why: Different human/robot carriers and sensor mounts exhibit distinct motion statistics and biases; a single learned motion prior generalizes unevenly.
papers.method: Depthwise/residual convolution encoder, cosine-prototype router with Gumbel softmax, four carrier experts, shared upsampling sequence decoder with bidirectional-LSTM velocity and variance heads; a cloned-state MSCKF combines velocity constraints. Unseen carrier adapts a new residual expert and router rather than all pretrained weights.
papers.math: Router weights alpha_i=softmax(sim(normalize(z),normalize(p_i))*scale/tau); fused temporal features sum_i alpha_i E_i(X). Predicted mean mu and softplus-positive variances feed a history-clone Kalman innovation. Prototype orthogonality and carrier-prior losses regularize the router.
papers.evidence: Primary arXiv paper reports average ATE reduction 40% and RTE-10s reduction 34% over cited baselines. Actual source modules and config inspected; no numeric result independently recomputed. A quadruped ATE row can be worse than TLIO despite favorable averages.
papers.limits: Multi-carrier generalization is conditional. Authors cite unknown carrier, unusual mount, severe bias and initially supervised adaptation. BiLSTM heads consume bidirectional window context, and latency is not necessarily zero-lookahead; 500-sample 200Hz window covers 2.5 s of signal, not automatically 2.5 s output delay.
papers.transfer: Small domain-specific residual expert or training-only motion balancing, tested on held-out device. Do not conflate odometry ATE with tilt RMSE.

papers.title: Attitude-Aided Linear Calibration of Triaxial Accelerometers
papers.authors: Yongqiang Yu; Tian Huang; Yipeng Yang
papers.why: Scale, axis misalignment and static accelerometer bias distort gravity observation and sensor-frame alignment.
papers.method: Attitude-aided analytic calibration solving an affine accelerometer calibration and gravity reference using five arbitrarily oriented static known-attitude measurements and a constrained system.
papers.math: An affine calibration can be written f_cal=M(f_raw-b), combined with known sensor attitudes R_i and a constant gravity vector. Identifiability and minimal measurement count are tied to attitude availability.
papers.evidence: arXiv abstract and metadata report minimum five static orientations with known attitudes; full equations/experiments not independently extracted in this review.
papers.limits: Requires external/trusted attitude during calibration. Does not prove unaided online gravity extraction under arbitrary acceleration.
papers.transfer: Improve pre-experiment sensor calibration with clearly recorded pose references; benchmark with and without calibration.

papers.title: Attitude Estimation Using Inertial and Barometric Measurements
papers.authors: Melone Nyoba Tchonkeu; Soulaimane Berkane; Tarek Hamel
papers.why: Highly accelerated flight makes tilt from accelerometer and gyro insufficiently constrained when velocity measurements are unavailable.
papers.method: Deterministic Riccati observer cascaded with a complementary filter, analyzed for almost-global asymptotic stability under uniform observability; nonlinear SO(3)xR^2 observer combines IMU inputs with barometer and magnetometer outputs for local exponential stability under stated conditions.
papers.math: The observer evolves on SO(3) with auxiliary vertical-motion states and extra sensed pressure. Observability and convergence hold only under the particular stated measurement channels and excitation conditions.
papers.evidence: Primary arXiv abstract reports simulated and real-flight evaluation and formal AGAS/LES claims; no independent proof check.
papers.limits: Barometer and, in the second formulation, magnetometer are additional sensors. Neither can be used to assert absolute unassisted six-axis tilt observability.
papers.transfer: Use as comparison of sensing assumptions and stability proof techniques; exclude from strict six-axis baseline.

papers.title: A Robust Transformer-Based Error Compensation Method for Gyroscope of IMUs
papers.authors: Xin Ye; Weijia Xing; Zhilou Yu; Jichen Chen; Qingyue Ma
papers.why: Nonlinear time-varying gyroscope bias/scale/noise causes cumulative integration drift despite correct quaternion kinematics.
papers.method: Transformer sliding-window temporal gyroscope error prediction with SO(3)-aware preintegration loss and robust rotation residuals.
papers.math: omega_corr=omega_m-delta_omega_theta(history); q_{k+1}=q_k tensor Exp_q(omega_corr dt); geometric residual penalizes integrated rotation disagreement on SO(3). Exact hyperparameters depend on the full implementation.
papers.evidence: Publisher claims mean orientation error 1.56° versus Gyro-Net 1.49° and describes it as better, although 1.56>1.49 for a lower-is-better metric; the reported ordering is inconsistent and no independent rerun resolves it.
papers.limits: Windowed historical dependence and integrated bias drift; published numerical claim requires correction or matched table context. No trainable repository verified.
papers.transfer: Explicit gyro residual/bias head with physical propagation, compared against implicit GRU memory on bias drift and cross-device tests.

papers.title: Time and Frequency Domain Analysis of IMU-Based Orientation Estimation Algorithms with Comparison to Robotic Arm Orientation as Reference
papers.authors: Ruslan Sultan; Steffen Greiser
papers.why: Time-domain tilt RMSE alone misses phase delay and tracking bandwidth, especially under rapid motion.
papers.method: UR5e robot arm with Bosch 6-axis IMU; compare indirect KF, Madgwick and complementary filters using slow-amplitude poses and fast generalized binary noise; compute time RMSE/MaxAE, frequency response, coherence and averaged equivalent time delay.
papers.math: Dynamic transfer function and phase/coherence quantify frequency-specific attenuation and lag. AETD relates measured phase delay to frequency under the paper's composite-frequency calculation.
papers.evidence: Open-access article concludes Madgwick and complementary filters have best overall time/frequency accuracy on studied motions; IKF worst on those metrics but lowest averaged equivalent time delay.
papers.limits: One controlled robot-arm apparatus and tuned filters; orientation reference/extrinsic calibration and frequency window affect interpretation. Different filters may optimize different bandwidth targets.
papers.transfer: Add frequency response, phase lag and transient delay to TG-DCM benchmarking, not only angular RMSE.

papers.title: Deep learning-aided Kalman filter for low-cost attitude estimation via angular accelerometer and gyroscope fusion
papers.authors: Chaoyang Zhai; Meiling Wang; Zhiheng Xiao; Zitian Xiong; Renjie Li
papers.why: Low-cost gyro signal inaccuracies accumulate; physically informative angular acceleration and adaptive covariance can constrain integration error.
papers.method: Two Kalman fusion designs for gyroscope and separate angular accelerometer, augmented by learned process/measurement noise covariance rather than manually tuned fixed matrices.
papers.math: Classical innovation K=P^- H^T(HP^-H^T+R)^-1 with learned positive noise matrix R or Q; angular acceleration observation is an additional physical sensor, not derivable without uncertainty from the gyro itself.
papers.evidence: Publisher abstract reports >17% estimation error reduction in selected turntable experiments. Methods and raw files not independently checked.
papers.limits: Requires a distinct angular accelerometer, so not an equal-sensor six-axis attitude competitor.
papers.transfer: Learned covariance mechanisms and turntable testing with explicitly declared hardware budget.

papers.title: Comparative Study on the Robustness against Gyroscope Bias of Rule-based and Machine-Learning-based Attitude Estimation Approaches
papers.authors: Ji Hoon Park; Chang June Lee; Jung Keun Lee
papers.venue: Journal of Sensor Science and Technology 34(2), 130-137 (2025)
papers.why: Biased gyroscope measurements stress physical filters and ML estimators differently, especially as bias patterns vary.
papers.method: Comparative experimental robustness analysis of rule-based and learned attitude estimation methods under gyroscope bias.
papers.math: Inject/observe omega_m=omega_true+b(t)+noise; compare tilt/angle error as bias increases. Exact test-bias distributions require full methods.
papers.evidence: Publisher full article with title, authors, DOI and 2025 date was located. Quantitative outcomes not independently extracted or rerun.
papers.limits: Method comparison is bound to chosen device, bias magnitude/time model, sensor motions and evaluation definition.
papers.transfer: Design explicit constant/random-walk bias augmentation and OOD bias-response curves for baseline GRU and proposed bias head.

papers.title: Debiasing 6-DOF IMU via Hierarchical Learning of Continuous Bias Dynamics
papers.authors: Ben Liu; Tzu-Yuan Lin; Wei Zhang; Maani Ghaffari
papers.why: Explicit time-varying accelerometer and gyro biases are difficult to train because direct bias labels are rarely available and are confounded with motion.
papers.method: Separate controlled Neural ODEs for gyro and accelerometer bias; causal backward-difference cubic-Hermite input interpolation; SO(3) Lie-group integration via local charts; hierarchical gyro-first then accelerometer training using pose ground truth.
papers.math: dot(b_g)=f_theta(b_g,omega_m,dot(omega_m)), dot(b_a)=g_phi(b_a,f_m,dot(f_m)); dot(R)=R[omega_m-b_g]_x. Optimize orientation pose-log residual then translational losses instead of direct bias labels.
papers.evidence: RSS peer-reviewed primary paper and arXiv HTML sections, RSS PDF first page and repo source network_for_BiadDy.py, Interpolation.py, lie_algebra.py and learning.py examined. No training executed.
papers.limits: No bias-GT labels does NOT mean no pose GT: each training interval uses pose-derived approximate initial bias; stationary startup calibration is assumed. EuRoC/TUMVI validation uses temporal 80/20 within training sequences (test sequences held out), and stochastic noise beyond deterministic bias drift is left as future work.
papers.transfer: Compare explicit slow bias against implicit GRU state under common six-axis tilt, independent device, bias jumps and cold-start conditions.

papers.title: A Large-Scale Empirical Study of Deep Learning for MEMS Gyroscope Bias Estimation
papers.authors: Hsiu-Chi Tsai; Chia-Tung Chung
papers.why: IMU bias architecture comparisons can be dominated by ground-truth construction, preprocessing, recording domains and cross-sequence leakage instead of learning architecture.
papers.method: Empirical study of MLP, LSTM, TCN and Transformer bias regressors with LOSO on EuRoC and TUM-VI, 17 random seeds per core setting, ablations of label denoising and SO(3) auxiliary regularization.
papers.math: Variance decomposition of experiment outcomes into dataset and architecture contributions; study reports approximately 97% variation attributable to dataset choice and <1% to model family, conditional on the two datasets and tested settings.
papers.evidence: Original full-text extraction was available through scholarly index, and engrXiv DOI/landing metadata verified. Authors report 2,811 runs, no benefit of tested physics regularization in 390 confirmatory runs, and label corruption effects larger than architecture effects. No independent numeric reproduction.
papers.limits: Non-peer-reviewed preprint; two datasets, different bias label construction: EuRoC batch-optimization labels vs TUMVI angular-rate GT differentiated from smoothed pose. Variance attribution is NOT a global result across all IMU sensing or tilt tasks; author order conflicts between PDF and publisher landing metadata.
papers.transfer: Treat label-process variation and hardware/domain shift as first-class experimental factors before increasing network size or claiming a physics auxiliary-loss novelty.
papers.metadata_note: EngrXiv DOI landing page lists Tsai then Chung; extracted preprint PDF title page lists Chung then Tsai. Use DOI landing page for bibliographic metadata and flag version discrepancy.

papers.title: DIODEM – A Diverse Inertial and Optical Dataset of kinEmatic chain Motion
papers.authors: Simon Bachhuber; Dustin Lehmann; Ive Weygers; Thomas Seel
papers.why: IMU motion-capture benchmarks may conflate attitude error, sensor-to-segment misalignment, rigid versus nonrigid attachment, repeated trials, optical-reference errors and evaluation dependence.
papers.method: Eleven continuous experiments of two five-segment kinematic chains with optical markers, five rigid and five foam-mounted IMUs. Published processing calibrates sensor S to body B and optical M to earth E. Source CSVs contain rigid/nonrigid IMU and optical per-segment quaternions; motion types are nested in continuous sessions.
papers.math: Rigid calibration maps f_B=R_BS f_S, omega_B=R_BS omega_S; optical segment orientation R_EB=R_EM R_MB. Segment tilt error requires comparing quantities in the same body frame. Dependence hierarchy: segment, motion, experiment session.
papers.evidence: Published open-access primary description reviewed in full (nature.com and EuropePMC full text); 11 experiments, ten IMUs, foam artifacts broadband and known alignment processing. Released TG-DCM table has 422 segments nested in 86 motions and 11 experiments. No physical raw-recording or HDF5 converter replay.
papers.limits: If a derived HDF5 set does not preserve exact frame/calibration/mounting identity, apparent tilt failures may not be attributable to learned estimator. Only eleven independent continuous experiment sessions; category and mounting metadata not traceable in released test HDF5 pipeline.
papers.transfer: Reconstruct DIODEM converter; verify rigid/foam, segment/frame, GT alignment, experiment clustering and per-motion p95 before claiming improved generalization.

papers.title: Observer Design for Optical Flow-Based Visual-Inertial Odometry with Almost-Global Convergence
papers.authors: Tarek Bouazza; Soulaimane Berkane; Minh-Duc Hua; Tarek Hamel
papers.why: Estimate gravity direction and body velocity using optical-flow measurements with geometric convergence guarantees rather than a trajectory-regression prior.
papers.method: Cascaded observer: optical-flow velocity-direction constraints and inertial measurements feed a persistently exciting Riccati observer for body velocity/gravity; a complementary SO(3) observer recovers attitude using estimated gravity and optional magnetic observation.
papers.math: Body vertical/gravity is an explicit S2 state; Riccati observer guarantees require persistently exciting visual output; SO(3) orientation is recovered up to its unobservable gravity-axis heading.
papers.evidence: Complete primary arXiv PDF text retrieved through scholarly connector; abstract and method reviewed. Stability and simulations are author claims, not independently proven/reproduced.
papers.limits: Uses optical flow; convergence theorem does not hold after removing visual inputs. No directly matched raw-six-axis-only tilt benchmark.
papers.transfer: Treat explicit body-gravity-state observer as prior art and identify exactly what a new six-axis correction provides beyond established Riccati/geometry mechanisms.

papers.title: Reduced Order Observers for Monocular Visual Inertial Odometry
papers.authors: Amel Abi; Mouaad Boughellaba; Miaomiao Wang; Abdelhamid Tayebi
papers.why: Recover gravity direction and velocity without estimating every visual landmark, while preserving explicit yaw/translation gauge and geometric convergence conditions.
papers.method: Construct output from optical bearing measurements and temporal derivatives, yielding a reduced six-dimensional LTV observer for gravity and body velocity. Recover attitude up to constant yaw and translation up to a world offset. Add bias for 12-D LTV extension with local stability under stated conditions.
papers.math: Coupled LTV observer dynamics for body velocity/gravity with gains from a Riccati equation; stability depends on visual bearing-derived output and uniform observability. Constant-yaw gauge remains.
papers.evidence: Primary arXiv PDF full text retrieved; claims include uniform global exponential stability for unbiased reduced observer and local bias-augmented stability under assumptions. No numerical replication.
papers.limits: Camera bearings, derivatives and excitation are essential; not direct six-axis-only attitude accuracy evidence. Modeling gravity as explicit state is not novel independently.
papers.transfer: Use as controlled geometric prior art for S2 observer, and state precisely the loss of guarantees when removing visual observation.

papers.title: Nonlinear Observer Design for Visual-Inertial Odometry
papers.authors: Mouaad Boughellaba; Abdelhamid Tayebi; James R. Forbes; Soulaimane Berkane
papers.why: Provide consistent almost-global navigation observer geometry rather than local-only linearized attitude filtering while maintaining known gauge directions.
papers.method: Construct an extended matrix Lie group unifying pose, gravity, linear velocity and landmarks. Decouple almost-global rotation observer and exponential Riccati translational observer; combine in cascaded stability analysis.
papers.math: Extended matrix Lie group SE_(3+n)(3) for gravity/velocity/landmarks with joint SO(3) geometry. Gauge remains global gravity-axis yaw and translation; global conclusions depend on visual-inertial observation model.
papers.evidence: Primary arXiv PDF body retrieved (indexed text truncated at 50k characters); author simulation and EuRoC experimental claims not independently recomputed.
papers.limits: Requires visual measurements; convergence cannot be claimed for arbitrary six-axis motion by removing bearing information. Full methods not individually rederived in this second pass.
papers.transfer: Explicit prior art for geometric observer with gravity and bias state; focus potential novel work on six-axis observation constraints and calibrated confidence.

papers.title: Equivariant IMU Preintegration With Biases: A Galilean Group Approach
papers.authors: Giulio Delama; Alessandro Fornasier; Robert Mahony; Stephan Weiss
papers.venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 10(1), 2025; first arXiv 2024
papers.why: Preintegration and bias propagation benefit from a consistent Galilean group structure rather than decoupling bias in Euclidean coordinates.
papers.method: Discrete-time bias-aware equivariant preintegration on the Galilean tangent-group construction, with coupled state/bias errors and covariance/Jacobian propagation; tested against classical formulations.
papers.math: Group-based preintegrated navigation state with bias-aware Lie error; bias Jacobian and covariance propagated within the chosen invariant error coordinates.
papers.evidence: Full open-access manuscript text inspected via scholarly extraction; numerical comparisons are author-reported and not independently executed.
papers.limits: Relies on established inertial mechanization and often additional pose/velocity factors in downstream navigation. Our velocity-closure integral is not novel preintegration.
papers.transfer: Adopt tested bias Jacobians/error propagation when changing a rolling preintegrator; do not claim group-consistent bias propagation as new.

papers.title: IMU Propagation as Preintegration
papers.authors: Jianzhu Huai
papers.why: IMU propagation and preintegration are often duplicated code paths despite encoding identical physical state updates.
papers.method: Demonstrate convention-independent equivalence between propagation and preintegration with bias Jacobians and covariance, including tests against GTSAM.
papers.math: Preintegrated relative rotation/velocity/position and propagated state share underlying discrete state-transition and noise-error Jacobians.
papers.evidence: Full source preprint extracted and read; validation against GTSAM is author-reported.
papers.limits: A methodological/integration note, not a six-axis attitude benchmark or new observable measurement. Confirms rolling preintegration is prior art.
papers.transfer: Use to validate numerical equality of prefix-integral and explicit relative-window implementations.

papers.title: Theoretical error modeling and analysis of strapdown inertial navigation system alignment under zero-velocity conditions
papers.authors: Hamed Mohammadkarimi; Mahdi Mobtaker; Mohammad Hossein Alizadeh
papers.why: Zero-velocity constraints and stationary alignment have orientation-dependent observability/precision limits that are hidden by idealized ZUPT narratives.
papers.method: Analytical navigation error model and observability study under zero-velocity updates with simulations and known-sensor field/stand validation.
papers.math: Linearized SINS error-state dynamics with velocity pseudo-observations; covariance and observability depend on IMU orientation, gyro/accel bias and sensor quality.
papers.evidence: Open-access primary article and scholarly indexed text read; experimental results are author-reported.
papers.limits: Stationary zero-velocity periods, high-grade IMU conditions and calibration assumptions; does not demonstrate equal nonzero velocity closure across active motion.
papers.transfer: Treat ZUPT+ESKF and calibration-dependent error bounds as mandatory close controls for interval-closure tilt.

papers.title: Time-domain features based zero-velocity detection for foot-mounted pedestrian inertial navigation system
papers.authors: Yanping Chen; Qiao Zhou; Jianpeng Li; Jun Zhou; et al.
papers.why: Traditional foot-stance ZUPT gates struggle with varying gait speed; reliably recognizing zero velocity can matter more than downstream filter architecture.
papers.method: Time-domain motion features detect foot zero-velocity intervals for SINS/ESKF navigation; authors report performance in field pedestrian trials.
papers.math: Zero velocity pseudo-observation v=0 constrains state via EKF update when stance detection is true; output depends on correct event classification.
papers.evidence: Publisher abstract and section snippets; full article code/parameters and experiments not independently obtained.
papers.limits: Foot-mounted gait and exact zero velocity; not an equal nonzero sensor-velocity closure model across arbitrary carriers.
papers.transfer: Match a normal ZUPT event detector and analyze false-closure risk on previously unseen motions.

papers.title: Intelligent zero-velocity detection with autoencoder fusion for enhanced foot-mounted human tracking
papers.authors: Yu Liu; Jun Zhou; Ruimin Song; Yanping Chen; et al.
papers.why: Learned motion state classification can improve foot-mounted zero-velocity detection over fixed IMU thresholds but remains distribution dependent.
papers.method: Time/frequency features, GLRT and convolutional autoencoder for foot stance / gait condition, then ZUPT correction in SINS.
papers.math: Fusion of a GLRT event likelihood and learned reconstruction features selects zero-velocity pseudo-observation updates.
papers.evidence: Publisher article abstract and highlights, author numbers not independently reproduced.
papers.limits: Foot-stance contact dynamics and environment-specific training; a learned ZVD event does not provide a deterministic physical guarantee.
papers.transfer: Use as a direct learned-event/GLRT comparator before claiming a novel closure detector.

papers.title: GaRLILEO: Gravity-aligned Radar-Leg-Inertial Enhanced Odometry
papers.authors: Chiyun Noh; Sangwoo Jung; Hanjun Kim; Yafei Hu; Laura Herlant; Ayoung Kim
papers.why: Foot slip and vibration degrade body gravity and vertical trajectory estimation in legged robots.
papers.method: Continuous-time fusion of radar Doppler-derived ego velocity, leg kinematics and IMU with a soft S2 gravity factor.
papers.math: S2 gravity factor coupled to velocity-aware continuous-time motion spline; radar/leg signals provide additional observations.
papers.evidence: Primary arXiv landing and indexed paper manuscript inspected; no code executed and journal numeric results not independently reproduced.
papers.limits: External radar and leg kinematics at runtime; not raw six-axis standalone tilt. S2 gravity factors not novel by themselves.
papers.transfer: Prior art for velocity-aided gravity, appropriate as an aided upper-bound, not same sensor-budget baseline.
